name: Maurice Schwabe
bio: The circle's connective figure and its most protected name: nephew by marriage of Sir Frank Lockwood, the Solicitor-General who prosecuted Wilde's final trial. Schwabe introduced Wilde to Taylor (Wilde's and Taylor's concurring sworn testimony), introduced Atkins to Taylor, and gave the Kettner's dinner at which Mavor met Wilde; Atkins placed him, 'a man of about twenty-two years of age,' in Wilde's bed in Paris in November 1892. At the trials his name was written on paper and passed to counsel rather than spoken; Wilde testified in April 1895 that Schwabe had been out of England for about two years, and he was never called.

bio_note: The General Index of Complete Letters (2000) contains no Schwabe entry — verified at the rendered index page (printed p. 1263, where the entry would fall between Schreiner and Schuster) — so no editorial 'main particulars' footnote exists there to cite. (The deeper catalogue record at collection.sl.nsw.gov.au returned HTTP 403 and was not read.) searched without result: McKenna, Secret Life (2008), PDF pp. 327-333, 547, 568, 586, 604 - the fullest narrative treatment in the repo, and it gives no dates; Laura Lee's blog posts under her 'Maurice Schwabe' category and her book page - no dates, and she notes that Schwabe 'did not leave any autobiographies or a large cache of his correspondence in an archive'; the Complete Letters OCR mirror, which contains no occurrence of the name at all, consistent with the earlier finding that the General Index has no Schwabe entry.
